change: board 425: the AP CSP pseudocode post in the news blog, one Matrixify Blog Posts row. Section I is 70 questions not about 40; REPEAT UNTIL checks before each pass, not after, in four places; 7 of 8 practice questions graded the wrong option and 2 printed the wrong key; list indexing, the Boolean operator count, the AND and CAN_MOVE rows, and a missing RANDOM(a, b). Plus the preflight rule that refused every Blog Posts sheet as a new page.
_context: NOTHING HERE REACHES A STUDENT UNTIL A HUMAN IMPORTS ONE SHEET.
Merging deploys the API and changes nothing the API does. The change that
matters is the import of imports/2026-09-25-csp-pseudocode-post/
csp-pseudocode-post-repair-blog-posts.csv, and the only way to know it
happened is to read the live article afterwards.
So scripts/verify-csp-pseudocode-post-live.js is written to be FALSE BEFORE
and true after, and it was measured both ways on 2026-09-25: against the live
page it reports 1 ok and 15 failed, the one being Q1, which was already right;
with --simulate-import, which splices the sheet body into the live page, it
reports 16 ok, including Chromium accepting the right answer on 8 of 8 where
the live page accepts 1. The simulation exits 3 and never prints the line
this manifest expects, so it cannot satisfy the live check.
THE REDERIVE IS PHASE PRE for the same reason as the FRQ archive manifest:
the generator is find-or-refuse, so once the repair is live it must refuse
to build. Before the import it is true evidence; after, the live check is
what re-derives.
THE SUITE RE-DERIVES THE KEY BY RUNNING THE PAGE'S OWN PSEUDOCODE through an
interpreter for the reference sheet subset the post uses, rather than
agreeing with a table somebody traced by hand. Hand tracing is how the page
got seven wrong keys. The interpreter is held to the post's five worked
outputs and to CED AAP-2.K.5 before it judges anything, and the sixth
mutation proves that self-check is load-bearing.

checks.name: re-derived keys, the repair, every checkBody rule broken alone, the sheet read back
checks._why: Offline against the before snapshot committed beside the sheet. Section 2 derives all eight answers by running the page's code; section 5 breaks each checkBody rule on its own and requires that rule, by name, to be the one that fires; section 6 requires the committed sheet to be byte-identical to a rebuild.

checks.name: the Matrixify preflight, including the Blog Posts case it used to refuse
the sheet rebuilt from the LIVE article, parsed back and diffed
checks._why: Fetches the article through lib/storefront-fetch.js, extracts the stored body from the theme wrapper, re-applies every anchored edit, and reads both sheets back off disk with a reader that did not write them. Every anchor must match the live body exactly once, so this also proves the page has not changed since the snapshot. PHASE PRE: after the import every anchor matches zero times and the build refuses, which is the stale-sheet guard working.
